newsitem.title: JAPAN: BOJ governor says policy aims at ensuring recovery.
newsitem.headline: BOJ governor says policy aims at ensuring recovery.

text.p: Bank of Japan (BOJ) Governor Yasuo Matsushita said on Tuesday that the BOJ's monetary policy is geared towards ensuring a firm basis for economic recovery.
He also told a budget committee of parliament that the effects of the central bank's easy monetary policy have been steadily filtering through the Japanese economy.
Japan cut its official discount rate to a record low 0.5 percent in September last year, and has generally kept money market rates at levels below the official discount rate.

"The effects of our easy monetary policy are steadily filtering through the economy," Matsushita said. Although bank lending growth remains rather weak, there are no worries over liquidity as seen in money supply figures, he added.
"Japan's economy is continuing its gradual recovery and the strength of the recovery is becoming more firm," he said.
However, Matsushita added that companies are adopting a cautious stance towards prospects for the economy.
"The current economic activity is expanding. We want to strengthen the favourable cycle where production, income and spending will all grow in an inter-related manner," he said.
"Our monetary policy will continue to aim towards securing a basis for economic recovery while keeping watch over economic developments," he said.

Matsushita said he realised that those depending on interest income for their livelihood, such as pensioners, have been hard hit by the central bank's easy monetary policy. But by adopting such a policy, the BOJ strongly hopes that the economy as a whole will revitalise and such positive effects will spread throughout, he said.
